own_solution.law: Photon energy E = hc/lambda = 3.1 eV; photon rate N = P/E; current I = eta N e = eta P / (E/e) = 0.003 * 5e-3 W / 3.1 V
assumptions: photoemission is energetically possible at 400 nm

T9477.regime: photoemission occurs while the work function is below the photon energy 3.1 eV (1.9 eV is inside)

TEBFE.regime: photoemission occurs while the work function is below the photon energy 3.1 eV (1.9 eV is inside)

notes: Base: E = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV = 4.9662e-19 J; N = 5e-3/4.9662e-19 = 1.0068e16 /s; I = 0.003 * 1.0068e16 * 1.602e-19 = 4.839e-6 A (e cancels: I = 1.5e-5/3.1 A). With 3.4 mW extra on the cathode: 0.003 * 8.4e-3/3.1 = 8.129e-6 A. Wall-chart lamps are shielded from the window (D); earlier-measurement sentences leave no state (D). Work function 1.9 eV is below 3.1 eV, so it matters only for the threshold (K); the stated yield already fixes the emission rate. Number check: all 3.4 mW sentences agree; both work-function sentences say 1.9 eV; T306C and TE41A are numeral-free.
